name: apple-design
description: Use for gesture-driven and physics-based interaction, springs, drag and swipe behavior, sheets, momentum, interruption, and Apple material or depth effects. Not for general typography, ordinary frontend work, accessibility review, or broad product critique.

name: code-review
description: Review changes since a fixed point along separate Standards and Spec axes. Use for branches, pull requests, work-in-progress changes, or "review since X" requests. Runs both axes through fresh Pi reviewers and reports them side by side.

name: codebase-design
description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

name: deslop
description: Remove AI-generated code slop from a branch — needless comments, defensive try/catch, `any` casts, over-nesting. Use when the user says "deslop", "remove the slop", "clean up the AI code", or wants AI-written code made to match the surrounding style.

name: diagnosing-bugs
description: Use for hard, elusive, intermittent, or performance bugs, or when a first repair attempt failed. Also use when Charlie explicitly asks for a full diagnosis or debugging investigation.

name: firecrawl
description: Use Firecrawl for an explicit Firecrawl request, site mapping, bulk crawling, structured web extraction, or live page interaction that Pi's native web and browser tools cannot provide. Do not use for normal search or reading a known URL.

name: grill-me
description: Stress-test a plan, decision, or idea through a structured interview. Use when Charlie asks to be grilled or wants relentless questioning before acting.

name: herdr
description: Control Herdr, a terminal multiplexer for coding agents. Use only when the user explicitly mentions Herdr or asks to use Herdr to inspect or control panes, tabs, workspaces, commands, or another agent. Do not use merely because a task could benefit from a background terminal, delegation, or parallel work. Requires HERDR_ENV=1.

name: impeccable
description: Design, redesign, critique, audit, or substantially improve a frontend interface. Use for product UI, websites, dashboards, components, forms, onboarding, responsive behavior, accessibility, UX copy, visual direction, and design systems. Not for backend-only work or a narrow micro-detail polish request.

name: make-interfaces-feel-better
description: Use for explicit UI polish and micro-detail work such as "make it feel better", "feels off", optical alignment, border radius, tabular numbers, icon weight, and motion restraint. Not for ordinary frontend work or whole-surface design, redesign, or critique, which belongs to Impeccable.

name: pango-dev-env
description: Invoke first for Pango backend-app local development or Charlie's production AWS reads. Use before running the app stack, tests, Artisan, Composer, npm, Tinker, pgcli, or AWS commands in a Pango worktree. Covers the branch-scoped pango CLI, reuse-only development slots, seeding, and safe environment ownership.

name: pdf
description: Use when tasks involve reading, creating, or reviewing PDF files where rendering and layout matter; prefer visual checks by rendering pages (Poppler) and use Python tools such as `reportlab`, `pdfplumber`, and `pypdf` for generation and extraction.

name: plain-writing
description: Write or revise Charlie's prose in his plain style: simple words, complete sentences, no dashes, jargon, analogies, or filler. Use for any prose drafted for Charlie and for requests to simplify, tighten, or reword text. Do not apply it to code.

name: pr-description
description: Write or edit a GitHub pull request title and description in the concise, plain convention Charlie prefers. Use whenever creating, opening, or updating a PR body or title (gh pr create, gh pr edit), or when asked to write, fix, or shorten a PR description.

name: prototype
description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

name: read-the-damn-docs
description: Use when an answer or implementation depends on a third-party library, framework, SDK, API, CLI, cloud service, provider, or other version-sensitive contract. Also use for current or official behavior and consequential auth, security, billing, data, migration, deployment, compliance, or privacy claims.

name: resolving-merge-conflicts
description: Use when resolving an in-progress Git merge, rebase, or cherry-pick conflict.

name: review-animations
description: Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

name: simplify
description: Read-only review for overengineering and avoidable complexity. Use when Charlie asks what can be deleted, whether code is overengineered, or requests a simplification review. Do not use for an ordinary implementation request that merely uses the word simplify.

name: skill-cleaner
description: Audit installed skills for duplicate ownership, stale triggers, prompt cost, and safe deletion.

name: tdd
description: Test-driven development. Use when the user explicitly wants test-first work, red-green-refactor, or asks to use TDD.

name: teach-me
description: Teach a topic in stages and check understanding before moving on.

name: writing-for-agents
description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

name: dev-note
description: Capture a local development decision or review note for the next PR tour.

name: ext-php-rs
description: Build PHP extensions in Rust with ext-php-rs. Use when binding Rust functions, structs, impls, constants, modules, interfaces, or PHP-visible APIs with ext-php-rs macros, especially in Laravel/PHP projects.

name: laravel-model-states
description: spatie/laravel-model-states — state machines on an Eloquent column. Use when transitions need library enforcement, per-state behavior, or transition classes as single writers.

name: pango-debug
description: Debug the Pango web app in a real browser with Agent Browser. Use when validating features live, reproducing UI bugs, testing the dashboard or `/chat`, or when an authenticated browser session against the local stack is needed.

name: pango-e2e-mockless
description: Write, run and debug the mockless end-to-end tests in web/tests/E2E (the e2e-live tier) against a real Shopify store, the real PostNord sandbox and a real receiver Lambda. Use when adding or fixing an E2E test, when `pango e2e run` fails, when reaching for a test primitive like poll/seededOrder/apiClient/submitReturnViaPortalApi, or when a change touches webhooks, carrier tracking, the returns portal or the release workflow and you need proof it works end to end.

name: pango-js-ts-style
description: Mandatory modern JavaScript and TypeScript style for writing and editing JS or TS. Use whenever producing JavaScript or TypeScript code.

name: pango-php-style
description: Mandatory PHP 8.5+ style for writing and editing PHP. Use whenever producing PHP code.

name: pango-rust-style
description: Mandatory modern Rust style for writing and editing Rust. Use whenever producing Rust code.

name: pr-tour
description: Build a PR tour, a single-file HTML review companion for a pull request. Analyze the diff, interview the author, write a spec, and generate a standard document the author posts in Slack next to the PR link. Use when someone asks for a PR tour, a review guide, or reviewer context for a branch or PR.

name: zen-jdm
description: Build business rules with GoRules Zen Engine 0.55 and JDM. Use when creating or evaluating JDM files, decision tables, expression or switch nodes, custom nodes, subdecisions, or the Enigma DecisionLoader and CustomNodeAdapter implementations.

name: monitor
description: Crash-safe non-blocking watcher for Pi. Own one bounded local process, observe an independently owned remote job with a read-only probe, or tail a log; receive conditional in-session pings without blocking.

name: pi-subagents
description:
Delegate work to builtin or custom subagents with single-agent, parallel,
scripted-chaining, async, forked-context, and coordinated workflows. Use
for advisory review, implementation handoffs, and multi-step tasks where a
single agent should stay in control while other agents contribute context,
planning, or execution.
